audio_caption: The clip begins with a male speaker introducing a module on AI-first engineering, specifically focusing on AI in banking within the context of deep learning. He mentions the modules are divided, leading into a discussion of what's happening to legacy banks. He notes that they might not be doing as well as they used to, but they are acquiring newer banks and have a plan to position themselves for the future. He says "I."

The audio clip begins with a male speaker introducing a "little summary of the types of AI" one might see in banking, including "natural language processing," "image analysis," and "robotic process automation."  He continues speaking with an analytical tone, discussing the differences between "predictive analysis" and "machine learning" and explains that this area is "using sophisticated analysis" to mine data from large numbers of numbers to infer things such as "which stock to buy," and mentions "harbingers" or someone about to default on a loan. He signs off and then the clip ends with the distinct sound of someone clearing their throat.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker introducing "a few news quotes." He mentions a date in January of this year and Lloyds, mentioning a closing announcement and bank closings. He cites a statistic about the number of bank branches closed in the United Kingdom and ATM reductions, attributing it to decreased cash usage. Further, he notes the increased costs of remaining ATMs due to the limited benefits they can derive from user activity. The speaker concludes that this trend is "hardly surprising."

The audio clip features a single male speaker with a measured tone. He discusses the shift from physical banks to digital electronic banks, noting that there are fewer reasons to visit banks in person due to the rise of electronic transfers. He acknowledges that there are still some reasons for physical banks, but not as many as there used to be.

The audio clip features one male speaker with a neutral speaking tone, discussing a story from December about an Italian bank cutting jobs and branches in favor of digital services, mentioning the usual problem of training staff. This is followed by the same speaker presenting statistics on Bank of America branches over the last 10 years, noting a steady decline of about 20% without significant recent changes.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker discussing bank closures in the United Kingdom, mentioning the Royal Bank of Scotland and Lloyds. He notes a higher rate of closures in the UK. Following this, a short burst of speech occurs which is indecipherable.

The audio clip features one male speaker discussing trends related to Citibank, highlighting the declining amount of contact with people at the bank and the growth in electronic statements and online banking. The tone is informative and descriptive. There's a brief pause.

The clip begins with a male speaker mentioning a "general statement" about AI and its impact on bank staff. He notes the general use of the term AI and suggests some applications are simply IT, referring to computers automating tasks previously done by people. The clip concludes with a short burst of speech from a second male speaker.

The clip starts with a male speaker stating, "according to that, this is that you should buy." He mentions Deutsche Bank cutting 18,000 jobs with another 200,000 possibly disappearing in the next decade. The speaker says it's not really AI but manual work and it's "still all part of the digitalization." He expands this to "of the industry," and further to "all industries."

The audio begins with a single male speaker, who has a neutral tone, talking about Goldman Sachs' reputation and its recent performance. The speaker mentions the Economist and suggests that Goldman Sachs didn't have a good strategy on AI and digitalization. He then compares Goldman Sachs' performance to other US banks, noting that European banks have done even worse. He states Goldman Sachs was profitable, unlike Deutsche Bank, which experienced a loss.

The audio clip features a male speaker in a conversational tone, beginning with "Okay folks" and transitioning into a discussion about job loss, specifically mentioning the Standard Bank's intent to reduce its headcount by 9%, which the speaker notes translates to a third of a million people. The tone remains informative and slightly concerned throughout.

The audio features one male speaker discussing the growth of Fintech and its impact on job losses, stating that "Fintech, which is this highly digital AI-oriented component of small startups," grew by "90%," and that this represents an increase of 37,000 jobs. He also mentions that Fintech is "only 5% of the legacy banks," suggesting that even with the job growth, it only accounts for 10% of the losses in traditional banking. The speaker has a serious, informative tone.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker discussing banks financing Fintech companies, summarizing it by saying "buy them up" leading to "a bank which is fintech enabled". The speaker appears to be explaining or analyzing a strategic approach, delivered in a conversational tone.

The audio clip starts with a single male speaker beginning a presentation with a neutral tone, stating "Okay, so here are the real numbers, 2022..." The speaker discusses an increase predicted for incumbents and an even bigger increase for Fintech, which may decrease by 2030 due to "the uh, 20 the virus". The speaker emphasizes the importance of this data as it provides a "solid picture" of how technology, AI, and big data may cause an "enhanced uh number of a certain type of job and a decrease in another type of job". The speaker concludes the presentation and says "Okay, that's the end of this module. Thank you."
